thread:
alice: Heads-up — regression spike on KV-int8 paths after ops-scheduler tweak. Seeing latency +18% p99 on small-chat workloads. Anyone else?
ben: saw that on nightly perf too. It only shows up when KV cache hit ratio > 0.65 and batches < 4.
charlie: interesting, do we have a repro? can we run the same load with fp8 KV to compare? :eyes:
alice: repro command I used: `./tools/prof/run_kv_quant.sh --model redwood-ggml-7b --mode int8-kv --seq 512 --qps 120 --workers 8`
ben: ran fp8 KV with same config: p50/p95/p99 = 7ms / 22ms / 43ms. int8-kv = 8ms / 26ms / 51ms. memory delta looks good (~-28% RSS on int8) but tail latency worse.
eva: attaching quick sample output from the profiler (truncated):
```
kv_hit=0.72 batches=3 worker=5 kernel=fp8_gemm
decode_tokens_per_sec=620
lat_p95=21.8
---
kv_hit=0.74 batches=3 worker=5 kernel=int8_gemm
decode_tokens_per_sec=590
lat_p95=25.9
```
frank: looks like kernel-selection jitter. ops-scheduler keeps switching between int8 and fp8 kernels when sequence length distribution crosses thresholds, which causes cache warm/cold churn on kernel contexts.
charlie: that would explain higher tail. Kernel warmup + CUDA kernel launch overhead + small-batch inefficiency. Can we force kernel pinning for a run to confirm?
alice: yes, added `--kernel-hint=pin:int8` and p99 dropped to 44ms (still slightly worse than fp8 pinned).
eva: quality check: decoding divergence is tiny — token-error-rate increase ~0.12% on one eval set, but we saw a handful of hallucination spikes on long prompts (seq>400).
ben: hypothesis: int8 KV quant introduces additional numerical noise that amplifies on long KV chains and interacts with async batching heuristics. small batches reduce amortization of that noise.
charlie: suggestion: tweak batching heuristic to prefer batching up to min(8, outstanding_requests) when KV hit ratio > 0.6. That should reduce kernel thrash.
frank: I want to try a hybrid approach: use fp8 kernels for KV read path (to preserve numerical stability) and int8 for compute-heavy MLPs. It costs some memory but might hit latency targets.
alice: can we run A/B overnight: route 20% traffic to hybrid, 40% to int8 pinned, 40% to fp8 pinned. We'll measure p99, memory, and token-error-rate.
eva: setting up CI job: `jobs/kv_quant_ab_test.yaml` with benchmarks + eval prompts. ETA results ~tomorrow morning.
ben: quick note — also saw a spike in kernel_scheduling_queue length during the throttle period, probably due to small batches accumulating. I'll add a metric to ops dashboard: kv_kernel_switch_count and small_batch_ratio.
charlie: also add a waveform trace for one slow request so we can see kernel switch timestamps.
alice: thanks team. main next steps: (1) run hybrid A/B, (2) add metrics and trace, (3) try batching tweak in sim env. If A/B shows quality regression >0.5% token-error we rollback. :thumbsup:
dev-bot: Deployment note: rolled back ops-scheduler v2 on prod-cpu-pool at 2145679920 — safe flag set.
frank: OK, once we have overnight numbers I'll open a short PR with the batching heuristic change and a reproducer script.
alice: appreciated — ping me if you need GPU time for hybrid runs.
charlie: FYI I'll also run a quant-calibration pass with per-head scale (instead of global) to see if int8 stability improves.
ben: great, thanks. keeping an eye on the dashboard. :eyes:
